title: GitHub and agency foundations
context: No GitHub account or Git knowledge is assumed. Priya needs evidence that the new developer understands why the agency uses version control and can move work from a secured account through fork, clone, branch, commit, push, PR, review, and merge.

stories.title: Create and secure a professional GitHub identity
stories.outcome: The learner owns a verified, protected account suitable for personal and client repositories.
stories.context: Create a free personal account using a durable email and professional username. Verify email, use a password manager, enable 2FA, save recovery codes outside the repository, and complete a basic profile.
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub email is verified and two-factor authentication is enabled
Profile name, short professional bio, and optional appropriate image are present
The learner explains why accounts are personal and why credentials/recovery codes are never committed or shared

expectations.security: Hide email addresses, 2FA secrets, recovery codes, and session details in evidence.
expectations.privacy: Public profile contains only intentionally public information.

stories.title: Complete the first repository, fork, and local workflow
stories.outcome: The learner can explain and perform the complete GitHub collaboration path.
stories.context: Begin with GitHub's browser Hello World exercise. Then fork the curriculum, install GitHub Desktop or Git, clone the fork, identify origin/upstream, and use disposable text files for conflict and recovery practice.
acceptanceCriteria: A browser-created practice repository includes README, issue, branch, commit, PR, review, and merge
The curriculum is forked under the learner account and the learner explains why changes do not alter the canonical repository
The fork is cloned locally and origin/upstream are identified
A practice PR contains at least three coherent commits
A merge conflict is resolved and its markers are explained
A safe commit is reverted and the original change is recovered through history

expectations.privacy: No employer repository or private code.

nonGoals: Memorizing the full Git command set

stories.title: Inventory and score ten software ideas
stories.outcome: Three right-sized project candidates are selected using evidence rather than excitement alone.
stories.context: Ideas are scored 1–5 for user pain, user access, smallest scope, security/data risk, API dependency, learning value, and client potential.
acceptanceCriteria: At least ten ideas are described in one sentence each
Every idea has all seven scores and a short rationale
One quick win, one API idea, and one database idea are selected
Deferred ideas include a reason and a condition for reconsideration
stories.dataContract: IDEAS.md table using the supplied idea-scorecard template.

expectations.security: Flag ideas involving regulated or employer data.
expectations.privacy: Use generalized descriptions when an idea involves a real person or employer.
expectations.analytics: Define one success signal per selected idea.

definitionOfDone: Selection rationale survives an AI critique

stories.title: Explain the agency GitHub workflow
stories.outcome: The learner understands why each GitHub object exists instead of following clicks by memory.
stories.context: Draw and narrate the path from a client story to local work, review, merge, deployment, and recovery. Include who owns each repository and when a fork is appropriate.
acceptanceCriteria: Diagram includes account, canonical repository, fork, clone, branch, commit, push, issue, PR, review, merge, and deployment
The learner explains what exists locally versus on GitHub
The learner explains a safe recovery path after a bad change

expectations.security: No tokens or private repository details.

definitionOfDone: Workflow can be explained without reading definitions
